chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Self-confidence and Dameron's arrangements as a challenge
summary: After ten professional years Moore talks about ego and confidence and the demanding arrangements of Tadd Dameron.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution

blocks.x: By this time you had been performing as a musician, well, professionally, over ten years and how did you feel about your progess and what you were doing musically?
Well, in a way, I was thinking of

New York again. I was getting more confidence in my playing. I was beginning to feel, you blow it, I can blow it, too. You've got to have that self-confidence us musicians have in order to compete in the field, you know. All of tremendous ego$ I think. You've got to have ego to make it one way or the other, you've got to have that ego and confidence in yourself. You've got to be able to compliment the other guy who out-blows you, you know, as well as the guy you outblew. You got to compliment him too, and praise him. That's the only way you'll get along with other musicians, as well as in life, non- and endeavor humble musicians, in every field of work/you must always feel at the same time within yourself and how you stand with the next fella, you have to believe in yourself.

Up to that time, whose writing and what compositions gave you the most in the way of a challenge, musically. That is in terms of their harmonic structure with their melody. Do you remember some of the tunes or the songs that were challenging to you that were challenging to you and you said, boy, I've really got to work a little harder on this to get the feeling right, to get the harmony straightened out, the harmony right?
At this point, in this era, I always marveled at the different arrangement structures and
